knowledge:
- key_parameters: gene.p=A named numeric vector of p-values from a bulk differential expression analysis, where names are gene symbols/IDs ;; marker.g=A list of marker genes for each cell type; if NULL, species and region must be specified to retrieve them from ExperimentHub ;; species=Species name (e.g., "mouse", "human") used for automatic marker retrieval ;; region=Brain region or tissue abbreviation (e.g., "FC" for Frontal Cortex, "pFC" for Prefrontal Cortex) used for automatic marker retrieval ;; method=Regression method to use; "LiR" for Linear Regression (used in LRcell) or "LR" for Logistic Regression (used in get_markergenes and LRcellCore) ;; expr=A read count matrix with rows as genes and columns as cells, used for custom enrichment score calculation ;; annot=A named vector of cell-type annotations, where names correspond to column names of expr ;; power=A hyper-parameter controlling the penalty for the proportion of cells expressing a certain gene ;; parallel=Logical indicating whether to execute enrichment score calculation in parallel ;; n.cores=Number of cores to use for parallel execution ;; topn=Number of top marker genes to select per cell type ;; min.size=Minimum number of marker genes required for a cell type to be included in LRcellCore ;; sig.cutoff=Significance cutoff for p-values/FDR in LRcellCore or plotting
- alternatives: LRpath=The original algorithm designed for pathway/gene set enrichment analysis which inspired LRcell ;; LRcell vs LRcellCore=LRcell is a wrapper that automatically retrieves marker genes from ExperimentHub based on species/region, whereas LRcellCore is the core function that requires a user-provided marker gene list
- when_to_use: Use this analysis when you have bulk RNA-seq differential expression results (gene p-values) and want to identify which specific cell types or sub-cell types are driving the observed transcriptional changes, especially when paired single-cell RNA-seq data for the same samples is unavailable.
- pitfalls: Using LRcellCore with logistic regression (method = "LR") might trigger convergence warnings (e.g., "Warning: glm.fit: algorithm did not converge") if the marker gene set or input p-values are highly skewed or small ;; The columns of the expression matrix (expr) must exactly match the names of the annotation vector (annot) when calculating custom gene enrichment scores ;; Ensure correct gene identifier matching (e.g., gene symbols) between the bulk DE p-values (gene.p) and the marker gene lists.

workflows.name: lrcell_preloaded_markers
workflows.intent: Run cell-type enrichment analysis on bulk RNA-seq differential expression results using pre-loaded marker genes from ExperimentHub.
input: example_gene_pvals.RData (named numeric vector of bulk DE gene p-values)
workflows.stages: 1. Load bulk DE p-values ;; 2. Run LRcell using linear regression with specified species and brain region ;; 3. Exclude leading genes for clean visualization ;; 4. Plot the enrichment results using a Manhattan plot.
workflows.code:
data("example_gene_pvals")
res <- LRcell(gene.p = example_gene_pvals,
              marker.g = NULL,
              species = "mouse",
              region = "FC",
              method = "LiR")
FC_res <- res$FC
sub_FC_res <- subset(FC_res, select=-lead_genes)
head(sub_FC_res)
plot_manhattan_enrich(FC_res, sig.cutoff = .05, label.topn = 5)

workflows.name: lrcell_custom_markers
workflows.intent: Run cell-type enrichment analysis on bulk RNA-seq differential expression results using custom marker genes derived from user-provided single-cell RNA-seq data.
input: example_gene_pvals.RData (named numeric vector of bulk DE gene p-values)
workflows.stages: 1. Calculate gene enrichment scores from the single-cell expression matrix and annotations ;; 2. Extract top marker genes for each cell type ;; 3. Run LRcellCore using logistic regression with the custom marker genes ;; 4. Curate cell types and visualize the enrichment results.
workflows.code:
enriched_res <- LRcell_gene_enriched_scores(expr = sim.expr,
                            annot = sim.annot, parallel = FALSE)
marker_res <- get_markergenes(enriched.g = enriched_res,
                method = "LR", topn=1)
res <- LRcellCore(gene.p = example_gene_pvals,
           marker.g = FC_marker_genes,
           method = "LR", min.size = 5, 
           sig.cutoff = 0.05)
res$cell_type <- unlist(lapply(strsplit(res$ID, '\\.'), '
[', 2))
head(subset(res, select=-lead_genes))
plot_manhattan_enrich(res, sig.cutoff = .05, label.topn = 5)
